headline: Colonial Pipeline ransomware shutdown disrupts U.S. fuel-product distribution
why_this_event_is_defensible: Clean refined-product bottleneck: the issue was gasoline, diesel, and jet-fuel distribution rather than crude supply. Testing UGA vs USO asks whether gasoline exposure moved differently from crude exposure.
what_would_falsify: UGA does not outperform USO; gasoline prices do not react; outage normalizes too quickly; broad oil beta explains the move.
operator_notes: Use 2021-05-10 as market date because the shutdown occurred Friday May 7 and Monday was the first full equity/ETF trading session after the news.

headline: U.S. moves ahead with steel/aluminum tariffs; domestic metal producers rally
why_this_event_is_defensible: Protective tariffs are a direct industrial-policy support for domestic steel producers. NUE (Nucor) is a replacement U.S. domestic-steel-producer proxy after the original primary (X / U.S. Steel) was unavailable in the local cache for this window; SPY controls for broader equity-market reaction to trade-war risk.
what_would_falsify: NUE does not outperform SPY; downstream cost concerns dominate; broad market/tariff-war risk explains the move better than domestic steel protection; NUE's mini-mill / electric-arc economics differ from X's integrated / blast-furnace economics enough that the tariff response is not directly comparable to the original ZIM-style framing.
operator_notes: Swapped primary from X to NUE because the local cache had no bars for X across the 2017-11-12 to 2018-07-30 window the preview asked for; NUE is the closest substitute U.S.-listed domestic steel producer with a different mill model (electric-arc rather than X's integrated process), so treat the row as a substitute steel-producer proxy rather than a like-for-like rerun of the original X-vs-SPY framing. Mechanism (producer protection from import tariffs) is preserved; benchmark unchanged. Coverage must still be checked before relying on the result.

headline: Federal Reserve temporarily excludes Treasuries and Fed deposits from SLR calculation
why_this_event_is_defensible: Clean capital-relief event: the rule reduces a leverage-ratio constraint on large banking organizations, supporting bank/intermediary balance-sheet capacity. KBE gives broad bank exposure.
what_would_falsify: KBE does not outperform SPY; credit stress dominates regulatory relief; move is indistinguishable from broad market rebound; no effect after FDR.
operator_notes: Source release was Apr 1 at 4:45 p.m. EDT, after market close, so use Apr 2 as the market event date.

headline: BIS imposes advanced semiconductor / supercomputing export controls targeting China
why_this_event_is_defensible: Direct revenue/access shock for advanced-chip exposure. NVDA is the clearest U.S.-listed single-name proxy; SMH controls for broader semiconductor-sector movement.
what_would_falsify: NVDA does not underperform SMH; market had already priced the restrictions; alternative demand offsets China restrictions; effect is sector-wide rather than Nvidia-specific.
operator_notes: Good interview event because it forces a ticker-vs-benchmark discussion instead of just semis down.

headline: Ever Given blocks Suez Canal, delaying oil, LNG, container, and consumer-goods shipping
why_this_event_is_defensible: Chokepoint/logistics disruption read using a longer-history container-carrier proxy. MATX is U.S.-listed marine shipping (Trans-Pacific routes — Hawaii, Guam, Alaska, China-California); IYT controls for broader transportation equities. The hypothesis is that a global container-rate spillover from the Suez bottleneck benefits a shipping-rate-sensitive carrier more than broad transports.
what_would_falsify: MATX does not outperform IYT; the Suez bottleneck does not lift rates outside the Asia-Europe lane MATX is not on; broad transport beta explains the move; rate firmness was already priced pre-event; event fades immediately after refloat.
operator_notes: Swapped primary from ZIM to MATX because ZIM IPO'd 2021-01-28, leaving no 60-bar pre-event estimation window for the 2021-03-24 event. MATX (Matson, NYSE) listed in 2012 after the Alexander & Baldwin spin-off, so the estimation window is recoverable from a standard daily-bar source. Tradeoff: MATX is not a pure Suez/container spot-rate proxy — its network does not transit Suez — so the read is an indirect spillover rather than a direct chokepoint read. Treat the row as a weaker test than the original ZIM-vs-IYT framing, not a stronger one. Coverage must still be checked before relying on the result.
